title: User Interface Dependency Conflict
definition: A situation where the user interface fails to load due to conflicts or incompatibilities between JavaScript dependencies.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Your app isn't working properly because it can't load some of its parts. This is like trying to put together a puzzle, but some pieces don't fit well with others.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: The user interface is experiencing a dependency conflict, likely due to incompatible JavaScript modules. This can prevent the page from loading properly and cause the websocket to drop.
difficulty_levels.expert: The issue is rooted in the interaction between the frontend and backend of the application. Incompatibilities between ES modules and CommonJS modules can lead to a failure to load JavaScript dependencies, which in turn causes the websocket to drop. This highlights the complexity of maintaining a cohesive user interface in a modern, modular software development environment.

extra_fields.insight: The root cause of the problem is a dependency conflict between JavaScript modules, which is preventing the page from loading properly.
